title: Italy beats China 2-1 in Billie Jean King Cup quarterfinals, advances to semifinals
dek: Italy defeated China 2-1 in the Billie Jean King Cup quarterfinals on Thursday in Shenzhen. Jasmine Paolini won both singles and doubles to secure the victory and send Italy, the two-time defending champion, to the semifinals against Ukraine on Saturday.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Jasmine Paolini extended her tournament winning streak to nine consecutive matches by beating Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen in singles and pairing with Sara Errani to win the doubles, clinching Italy's advance.
bottom_line: Italy and Ukraine meet Saturday for the second consecutive year in the semifinals. The winner advances to Sunday's final, where the ultimate champion will be decided in a best-of-three tie format.
body:
Italy defeated China 2-1 in the Billie Jean King Cup quarterfinals on Thursday in Shenzhen, with Jasmine Paolini winning both singles and doubles to clinch advancement for the two-time defending champion. Italy will face Ukraine in the semifinals on Saturday, with the final scheduled for Sunday.
China took an early 1-0 lead when Zhang Shuai defeated Elisabetta Cocciaretto 6-0, 6-2. Paolini then beat Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen 6-3, 7-6 (4) in the deciding singles match, tying the tie at 1-1. Paolini and Sara Errani clinched the victory with a 6-3, 5-7, 6-3 win in doubles over Guo Hanyu and Jiang Xinyu. Per ESPN's reporting, this was Paolini's ninth consecutive match win in the tournament.
Ukraine advanced to the semifinals for just the second time, defeating Belgium 2-1 earlier Thursday. Seventh-ranked Elina Svitolina was upset by Greet Minnen, ranked 217th.  Anhelina Kalinina gave Ukraine a 1-0 lead with a 6-7 (6), 6-1, 6-1 win over Jana Otzipka. Kalinina and Lyudmyla Kichenok then beat Magali Kempen and Lara Salden 6-3, 6-3 in doubles to secure Ukraine's passage.
Czech Republic beat Britain 2-0 in their quarterfinal. The Czechs are on course for a 12th title in the competition previously called Fed Cup. The United States did not qualify for the finals but holds a record 18 titles in the event.
